source_coverage_note: Original collection checked 14 source URLs and reported 3 source failures. Publisher opened the Tohoku and AISIN first-party announcements and the author forum; the exact IFParse v2 dataset card was unavailable to this review, although its listing was indexed.

candidates.title: Tohoku–Aisin 16 nm STT-MRAM AI SoC
candidates.summary: Joint university-industry research prototype with 32 MB embedded nonvolatile STT-MRAM and Tiny YOLOv3 object detection. Authors report a 65.7 ms boot, 50.7 mJ per frame and an approximately 25-fold whole-system speedup relative to their chosen comparison.
candidates.limits: Demonstration is not commercial availability or a general hardware benchmark. Claimed energy and latency depend on baseline, model, weights and memory architecture; no independent chip replication or public developer runtime was located.
required_before_import: Identify exact publication/conference proceedings and baseline measurement conditions
Clarify prototype status, software/runtime access and IP availability
Create stable technology profile and working search, relationships and detail route

candidates.title: IFParse v2.0
candidates.summary: Author-described synthetic 1,800-task benchmark measuring exact JSON transformation from nine telemetry grammars; distinguishes parseable JSON from completely correct field values and nulls.
candidates.limits: The dataset card and pinned README were not independently retrievable in this review. Author-reported scores on Qwen models have not been reproduced; the test set is public and may be contaminated, and deployment validity remains unmeasured.
required_before_import: Read a pinned dataset README and verify row counts, schemas, splits and licenses
Reproduce exact-match scoring on held-out examples or explicitly mark results unreplicated
Document contamination risk and evaluation harness before publishing a stable catalog profile

candidates.title: Spin-transfer-torque magnetoresistive RAM (STT-MRAM)
candidates.summary: Nonvolatile magnetic memory in which a spin-polarized current switches storage magnetization. Distinct from the speed of reading data (memory bandwidth), and not a universal substitute for GPU HBM.
candidates.limits: Memory cell design, power, write endurance and manufacturing cost vary by process; a successful specialized chip is not a universal performance guarantee. This is an established term newly proposed for Atlas, not a newly invented 2026 technique.
required_before_import: Check canonical dictionary aliases and source registry for duplication
Add stable term ID with source, mechanism, tradeoffs and worked example
Regenerate direct page, relationships, search index and manifests

candidates.title: Near-memory computing (NMC)
candidates.summary: Computing with processors and accelerators placed physically near memory so transfers can be shortened. Unlike processing-in-memory, computation need not occur inside the memory array.
candidates.limits: Benefits vary with workload access pattern, data reuse and on-chip capacity; a press-release reduction against one architecture cannot establish superiority across all models. This is not a November 3 invention.
required_before_import: Independently verify near-memory versus in-memory terminology and existing aliases
Document concrete memory-traffic comparison and the conditions where it helps
Publish stable sourced term page plus backlinks, relationships and search
